_readme: Street Scene driving parameters: the ONE file that holds every car physics number.

base: the shared tuning every car starts from (a front inline 6, rear wheel drive; the retired Proto Compact drove on it, and the physics tests drive it as is through baseTuning() in tests/helpers.ts).

cars.<id>: per car overrides, merged over base. Write absolute values (e.g. "mass": 2000), only the keys that differ. Nested objects merge key by key, arrays (torqueCurve, ratios) replace the whole array.
Keys starting with _ are comments and are ignored. Unknown keys fail loudly at startup, so typos never go unnoticed.
drivetrain.layout is "rwd", "awd" or "fwd". awdFrontShare is the AWD torque share sent to the front axle (0.4 = 40/60).

setup: the garage Tune tab's four sliders (suspension, gear ratio, differential, brake balance), five positions each with position 3 the stock car. applyBuild() in build.ts lays them over the car tuning.
Geometry (wheel positions, size) comes from src/assets/carManifest.json, not from here.
Physics tuning panel (Settings > Developer > Debug mode): Copy JSON exports `fileOverride`, a block you can paste into cars.<id> here. Editing this file discards stale tuning saved in the browser.

drivetrain._: diffOpen and diffLock are the driven axles' differential (car.ts updateAxles), 0 and 0 for the stock axle; the Tune tab's Differential slider adds to them (setup.differential).

gearbox._: The selectable cars set their own ratios and final drive (cars.<id>.gearbox), each top gear running into its limiter at about the car's slipstream top speed, 1.1 times its drag top speed (docs/handling.md, Gearing); these generic ones are base's. torqueBonus is the Gear Ratio slider's arcade term, 0 here (applyBuild writes setup.gearing.torqueBonus): extra engine torque, full up to torqueBonusFadeStart and gone by torqueBonusFadeEnd (m/s: 140 and 200 km/h), so it shapes corner exits and never the drag top speed.

tires._: Grip in ordinary corners comes from the rise to the peak, the slides from past it (docs/handling.md). roundingRear above roundingFront makes the rear answer sooner, so the car is stable below the limit even with gripRear under gripFront; that lower rear peak still lets go first at the limit, which is where the drifts start.

traction._clutch: clutchKickSpeed and drift.clutchKickTime are the throttle stab clutch kick (a lift then a stab while steering hard): 0 and 0, off. On a keyboard every throttle tap mid drift fired it and shoved the car along its nose; the handbrake is the clutch kick now (it drops the clutch on the revving engine, handbrakeDump of the way to the flywheel's speed, car.ts dumpClutch).

launch._: Launch control (car.ts): the two-step rev cut on the grid, line lock burnouts (gas and brake, or gas and the antilag button, standing) and rolling antilag (its own held button, with the gas, rolling; a press held on from a line lock stays a launch). twoStepRpm is the build's Launch RPM (0 = off); applyBuild writes it, so leave it 0 here. Off the line it is the launch clutch's slip rpm (with engine.launchRpm as the floor), so a launch never drops the revs it was held at and never meets the cut. lineLockRearShare is an arcade term: an AWD car sends that share of its front drive to the rear while line locked, so the front brakes hold it and the rear lights up (1 = all of it, 0 = its own split). defaultRpm is the car's stock pick, the Launch RPM a new garage build (or a saved one from before launch control) starts on; 0 = off. Set per car from what owners of its donor launch at. antilagRpm is the car's stock rolling antilag rpm, a separate setting from the two-step as on the ECUs that have both (Haltech's Rolling Anti-lag holds its own fixed limit): a build's Antilag RPM (the Tune tab, turbo cars only) replaces it, 0 = off. Hold it where the turbos are on full boost and the engine near its torque peak, so the release pulls at once.

steering._counter: Counter steer (steering into a slide): full lock is counterLockDeg, a drift angle kit mapped linearly from the input, or the ordinary lock plus counterSteerAllowance of the slide angle, whichever is more (car.ts counterSteerLock). Through an ordinary drift (under about 24 degrees at drift speeds) that is the fixed 38: a held key (full lock on a keyboard) does not point the front wheels past the direction of travel and pull the car outward, as 45 did. Past it the lock reaches beyond the slide, because a front wheel only catches a slide when it points past the direction of travel: with the fixed 38 alone a slide past 40 degrees swung on to 75.

nitrous._overdrive: Style past a full tank fills overdrive (car.ts fillNitrous), up to overdriveCap stages of it: it burns alongside the tank at the same rate and multiplies the burning stage's power by overdrivePower, so a full tank is worth topping up. A hit on a wall, barrier, rail or another racer at crashMinImpact m/s or harder (normal impact speed; both cars in a crash pay) loses nitrous, overdrive first: crashLoss stages at crashFullImpact and over, linear between.
nitrous._resetLoss: Share of the tank and overdrive a reset (the reset key, the stuck and lost resets, a tow off the tracks) costs: 1 empties both, 0 makes resets free (reset.ts relocateCar).

drift._: The aids (docs/handling.md, Simcade): yawDamping is always on, the same in a slide as on the grip, so the car's rotation answers the same way at any angle; the anti spin aid (assistTorque) only acts past maxSlipDeg, when the car is going round.

surface._quay: A harbor's quay (districts/waterfront.ts): dusty, oil stained dock concrete. A shade under the road's grip, so the yard and its skid pad slide a little earlier than the street beside it, and a small rolling drag from the grit, about a third of the cobbles'.
surface._sand: A beach's sand (districts/waterfrontBeach.ts): the off road section of the waterfront. Loose and slidey, a little better than dirt's grip (offroadGrip 0.49) and with less drag than it (offroadDrag 900): it bleeds speed hard enough that the boardwalk is the fast line and the sand a detour for the dune jumps and the drift strip, but a racer who commits to it is not stranded. The boardwalk's planks drive as cobbles (cobbleGrip, cobbleDrag).

wendtStrom._name: Wendt Strom (Golf R32 Mk4 donor): front naturally aspirated VR6, all wheel drive biased to the front (a Haldex coupling sends the rear its share). No boost: torque builds to a broad plateau around 3,000 rpm and fades gently to a 6,800 rpm redline.

gearbox._: The R32's six speed: 3.36 / 2.09 / 1.47 / 0.87 / 0.73 as listed for the Golf R32 (fourth, not listed, at 1.10). The final drive puts sixth's limiter (247 km/h) just over the slipstream top speed (244): the drag top speed (224) comes at 92% of the redline.

launch._: R32 owners launch near the VR6's torque peak (2,800 to 3,200 rpm); the DSG cars' launch control is reported at 2,500 to 3,500. An NA engine on an AWD grip launch wants the plateau, not more: the cut bounces it 3,150 to 3,500.

kazamaRotor._name: Kazama Rotor (RX-7 FD donor): front sequential twin turbo twin rotor, rear wheel drive. The lightest car: the primary turbo fills the low range, the secondary takes over near 4,500 rpm and it pulls to an 8,000 rpm redline; five speeds.

gearbox._: The FD3S five speed's first four gears (3.483 / 2.015 / 1.391 / 1.000) and the Type RZ's 4.300 final drive. The donor's 0.719 fifth is an overdrive for its 250 km/h; this car tops out against more drag (234), so fifth is 0.88: the drag top speed comes at 7,365 rpm, on the power plateau, and the limiter (261) just over the slipstream top speed (253). The old 0.72 left the top speed at 73% of the redline, where shorter gears went faster.

launch._: FD owners on the stock sequential twins report a weak, boostless launch around 4,000 rpm (the turbo handover) and better ones from about 5,000; past 7,500 is called abuse. 5,000 clears the handover without lighting up the rear tires of the lightest, RWD car.
launch._antilag: Rolling antilag at the 13B-REW's torque peak (5,500): a clear 1,000 rpm past the sequential twins' 4,000 to 4,500 handover, so both turbos are lit when the brake comes off.

albrechtKombi._name: Albrecht Kombi (1992-95 Audi S2 Avant donor): front 2.2 L 20 valve turbo inline five (ABY), all wheel drive split evenly (a Torsen centre differential). 230 PS (169 kW) at 5,900 rpm and 350 N·m from 1,950 to 3,000 rpm behind one KKK K24 turbo, a six speed manual, about 1,480 kg. A fat low rpm plateau and a long tail; the longest car, a little more yaw inertia.

gearbox._: Audi's 01E six speed as the RS2 (CRB) carries it and the S2's CGR is listed, 3.500 / 1.889 / 1.320 / 1.034 / 0.857 / 0.711, on the quattro 37:9 = 4.111 final drive. Sixth at 0.711 on the 4.111 gives about 40 km/h per 1,000 rpm, the 24.7 mph per 1,000 rpm S2 owners quote for a stock ABY. Sixth's limiter (6,600 rpm, 257 km/h) sits 10% over the drag top speed (234; the real car does 246 to 250: the sim's drivetrain and rolling losses take more than the real car's, so the top speed is held 5% under rather than lifted with a drag below the real figure), as on the other cars; the Gear Ratio slider's test needs the limiter that close (Short puts it at 0.92 of the drag top speed through a 1.2 final drive). aero.drag 0.36 is the real wagon's (Cd about 0.31 on 2.0 m2, 0.5 x air density x Cd x area = 0.37). torqueMul 0.94 on the real S2 torque shape lands the 0-100 on 5.8 s (the real 5.9). The shift rpm is the default 0.93 of the redline (6,140), just past the 5,900 rpm power peak where the real car would be shifted.

launch._: S2 launch practice is a clutch dump at 3,500 to 4,000 rpm, where the K24 is on boost (it is full at 1,950); the even AWD split takes the torque.
launch._antilag: Rolling antilag at 4,000: the K24 turbo is long past its lag there, with the plateau still 335 N·m and room in the gear for the pull.

daltonFiend._name: Dalton Fiend (2018 Dodge Challenger SRT Demon widebody donor): front supercharged 6.2 L cross-plane Hemi V8, rear wheel drive. 808 hp and 717 lb-ft on pump fuel (840 hp and 770 lb-ft on race fuel), a wall of low-rpm torque from the 2.7 L blower and a 6,500 rpm redline. The heaviest, longest, loosest car: the strongest straight line of the four, paid for in corners.

gearbox._: ZF 8HP90 first gear 4.71 on the Demon's 3.09 final drive, then a closer spread than the real 3.14 / 2.10 / 1.67 / 1.29 / 1.00 / 0.84 / 0.67 (that box reaches 300 km/h and more, far past this city's drag top speed, so its real overdrives would put the limiter near 420). Second and third (3.4 / 2.2 / 1.7) are a little taller than the donor's so the shift into third falls well short of the 60 mph mark at every Gear Ratio position; with the real 3.14 it fell on the mark and the Short box clocked a slower 0-60 than the next one. Eighth's limiter (261 km/h) sits 9% over the drag top speed (242), which comes at 92% of the redline. Drag is the real figure on the same scale as the other cars (aero.drag is 0.5 x air density x Cd x frontal area in N per (m/s)^2: a widebody Challenger's Cd of about 0.39 and 2.45 m2 give 0.57, against the Golf's and S4's 0.40 to 0.42). torqueMul 0.8 on the real 970 N·m is still far more thrust than the other cars have, so the torque curve falls away steeply above 5,000 rpm: the pull is in the low and mid range that decides the 0-100, and the little left at the top meets the drag. brakes.force is raised for the mass, and the rear tires are kept weak enough that rear brake bias still lengthens the stop. nitrous.force (the base 5,500 N) is scaled by the mass over the Wagon's 1,550 kg to about 7,600 N (a little over the mass ratio, so the Short box clears 1.25 times the dry top speed on nitrous), a bigger shot for the heavy car, so nitrous gives it the push the others get (the Short box still runs well past its limiter).

launch._: The Demon's TransBrake holds the car at about 2,350 rpm on its 315/40R18 drag radials; the Tune tab's launch picks come in 250 rpm steps from 2,500, so the stock pick is the first step, where the supercharged V8 is already past 900 N·m and the 1,940 kg hold the rear tires down.
launch._antilag: Off: a supercharger has no lag to bridge (the blower is at full boost off idle), and the Tune tab offers rolling antilag to turbo cars only.

nakayaHorizon._name: Nakaya Horizon GT (1997 Nissan Skyline GT-R R33 V-Spec donor): front twin turbo 2.6 L inline six (RB26DETT), ATTESA E-TS all wheel drive. 280 PS and 368 N·m at 4,400 rpm to an 8,000 rpm redline, a five speed manual, front heavy (57/43) and 1,540 kg. Drives like a rear wheel drive car until the rears slip, then the front axle takes its share.

gearbox._: The R33 V-Spec's Getrag 233 five speed, 3.214 / 1.925 / 1.302 / 1.000 / 0.752, on the real 4.111 final drive, with fifth at 0.893 instead of the real 0.752 overdrive: the R33 is governed at 180 km/h and reaches about 250, so its 316 km/h redline in fifth is far past this city's drag top speed (242). Fifth's limiter (266 km/h) sits 10% over it, as on the other cars, and the drag top speed comes at 91% of the redline.

launch._: RB26 owners launch at 3,500 to 4,500 rpm: the twins are near full boost by 3,000 and the ATTESA front axle shares the torque once the rears slip.
launch._antilag: Rolling antilag at 4,500: past the twins' full boost (about 4,000 rpm), near the torque peak.

tachibanaZenith._name: Tachibana Zenith (1994 Toyota Supra MK IV Turbo donor): front sequential twin turbo 3.0 L inline six (2JZ-GTE), rear wheel drive. 280 PS and 431 N·m at 4,000 rpm, a flat torque curve from 2,500 to 5,000 rpm to a 7,000 rpm redline, a six speed manual, 1,510 kg. Everything is there from low revs, so it launches hard and the rear tires pay for it.

gearbox._: The JZA80's Getrag V160 six speed, 3.827 / 2.360 / 1.685 / 1.312 / 1.000 / 0.793, on a 3.800 final drive (the real 3.133 with the real tire is a taller car than this city's drag top speed of 241 km/h can use), with sixth at 0.876 instead of the real 0.793 overdrive: the real sixth redlines at 356 km/h, so sixth is shortened until its limiter (266 km/h) sits 10% over the drag top speed, as on the other cars. The final drive is as low as that allows, so the Short gear setting keeps the same number of shifts through a corner exit as stock.

launch._: 2JZ-GTE owners launch at 3,500 to 4,500 rpm: the sequential twins are on boost by 2,500 and the torque is all there, so more revs only light up the rears.
launch._antilag: Rolling antilag at 4,500: past the twins' full boost, just over the torque peak.

tachibanaRunabout._name: Tachibana Runabout (1996 Toyota MR2 SW20 donor): mid mounted turbo 2.0 L inline four (3S-GTE), rear wheel drive. 245 PS and 309 N·m at 3,200 rpm, a wide plateau to 5,500 and a 7,200 rpm limiter, a five speed manual, 1,270 kg. The engine sits behind the seats, so the mass is gathered about the middle: it turns in quickly, the rear carries more of the weight and lets go when it does, all at once.

gearbox._: The SW20 Turbo's E153 five speed, 3.230 / 1.913 / 1.258 / 0.918 first four gears, on a 4.600 final drive (the real 4.285: a little shorter, so the Short and Long gear settings move a corner exit by the same 5% as on the other cars). Fifth is 0.694 against the real 0.731, which keeps fifth's overall ratio within 2% of the real car's (3.19 against 3.13) and puts the limiter (249 km/h) 10% over the drag top speed (225), as on the other cars.

launch._: SW20 Turbo owners launch around 4,000 to 5,000 rpm: the CT26 is on boost by 3,200, and the rear tires carry the engine's weight, so the mid engine hooks up better than a front engined RWD car would.
launch._antilag: Rolling antilag at 5,000: past the CT26's full boost, a little above the torque plateau's start.

swaps._: The garage Power tab's engine swaps, per car: swaps.<carId>.<swapId> is an override merged over that car's tuning (cars.<carId> over base) when a build fits the swap (build.ts applyBuild, before the setup sliders). Same rules as cars: absolute values, arrays replace whole, unknown keys throw. The swapped engine's layout, aspiration and voice are the manifest car's engineSwaps (src/assets/carManifest.json), which must list the same ids in the same order. Donor data and what is estimated: docs/carEngines.md, Wendt Strom engine swaps.

vr36._name: 3.6 VR6 (BWS, the Passat R36's): the 3.2's narrow angle six bored to 89.0 mm and stroked to 96.4 (3,598 cc, a 10.6 degree V), naturally aspirated. 300 PS (220 kW) at 6,600 rpm and 350 N·m from 2,400 to 5,300. The curve runs through those points (319 N·m at 6,600 is the power peak); the 6,900 redline is an estimate. About 10 kg over the 3.2 (estimate). torqueMul stays the car's 0.86, so the gain over the 3.2 is the real one.

turbo07k._name: 07K 2.5 turbo: the Mk5 Jetta and Rabbit's 2,480 cc inline five (82.5 x 92.8 mm, chain driven DOHC 20 valve, iron block; 170 hp at 5,700 and 240 N·m at 4,250 stock) on stock internals with a big single turbo on a T3 top mount manifold and an external wastegate, about 20 psi: 440 PS at 6,500 and 540 N·m at 4,500, the torque the stock rods are trusted with (an estimate: kits are sold for 400 to 500 hp). The big turbo is lazy: little under 3,000, the boost arriving through 3,500 to 4,500, so a longer spool and more of the torque behind it than the stock turbo cars. Rev limit 7,300 (034Motorsport's turbo tune raises the 07K's to that). Iron block plus the turbo, intercooler and piping: about the VR6's weight.

launch._: A big turbo wants revs at the line: 4,500 is where it is on boost, so the launch and rolling antilag both sit there.

daza._name: 2.5 TFSI (DAZA, EA855 evo, the 2017-20 RS3 8V's): 2,480 cc inline five (82.5 mm bore, the 07K's dimensions), aluminium crankcase, port and direct injection, one turbo. 400 PS (294 kW) from 5,850 to 7,000 rpm and 480 N·m from 1,700 to 5,850, a flat line to the power plateau: 401 N·m at 7,000 is the power at its end. Rev limit 7,200 is an estimate (the power plateau ends at 7,000). Audi gives it 26 kg under the iron block CEPA (183 kg), so about 25 kg under the VR6 (an estimate). Quick spool: a short lag behind a small share of the torque.

launch._: RS3 launch control holds about 4,000 to 4,500: full boost and the plateau. Rolling antilag at 4,500.

setup._readme: The garage Tune tab's four sliders (applyBuild() in build.ts lays them over the car tuning). Each table holds one entry per position, left to right (1..5). Position 3 is the stock car: every *Mul table holds exactly 1 there and every other table 0 (tuning.ts throws otherwise), so a stock build is bit for bit the car's own tuning and the AI, stock replays and bests are unchanged.

suspension._: Soft (1) to Stiff (5). Springs (frequencyMul on suspension.frequency) and travel to the bump stop (travelMul): soft leans more and rides over kerbs on long travel, stiff sits flat but bottoms out (sparks) on a kerb taken at speed. steerRateMul: how quickly the front wheels turn in. Grip: roadGripMul on the tires (tarmac and paving), roughGripMul is the grip on dirt, grass and cobbles relative to stock, where soft keeps the tires on the ground and stiff skips over it.

gearing._: Short (1) to Long (5), real gearing plus one arcade term (docs/handling.md, Gearing and Simcade). finalDriveMul moves the final drive, and with it the top gear's limiter, which on every stock car sits at its slipstream top speed: Short puts it at 0.92 of the drag top speed (a lower top speed on the limiter, nitrous runs into it sooner), Long at 1.3 (room for nitrous to keep pulling past the stock limiter, while the drag holds the dry top speed within 2.5% of stock). firstGearMul moves the overall first gear and the gears between blend evenly, so first stays put while Short closes the ratios up and Long spreads them out (lazier through the gears). An automatic keeps the revs in the same band at any final drive, so real gearing barely moves acceleration; torqueBonus is the arcade term that does: extra engine torque, full up to gearbox.torqueBonusFadeStart and gone by torqueBonusFadeEnd (car.ts), so short gears sharpen corner exits and long ones soften them without moving the drag top speed.

differential._: Open (1) to Locked (5), added to the car's drivetrain.diffOpen and diffLock (car.ts updateAxles; 0 and 0 is the stock axle, which turns both wheels together like a well behaved limited slip). open: an open differential gives each wheel the same torque, so drive past twice what the lighter wheel holds breaks that wheel loose and the axle passes on only twice its sliding force; open is how far of the way there. Stable, but drive fades as a corner lifts the inside wheel and a powered slide dies. lock: the force pair a locked axle makes in a turn while it grips, as a share of the axle's grip at the peak slip: it resists the rotation (push on turn in, steadier and harder drive out of a turn) and uses up the inside wheel's grip, so once the axle lets go both wheels spin together and hold the slide as the stock axle does.

brakeBalance._: Rear (1) to Front (5): frontBiasAdd moves brakes.frontBias. Rear bias makes the rear tires do more of the stopping, which costs them side grip and rotates the car on the brakes (trail braking into a slide) but locks the lighter rear sooner (longer stops); front bias stops straight and stable on grippy tarmac.

traffic._: Ambient traffic (src/sim/traffic.ts): civilian cars driven kinematically along street lanes, keeping right, and solid passive bodies once struck. Speeds m/s, accelerations m/s^2, lengths m, masses kg.
traffic._loose: A struck car slides: lateral speed bleeds off at slideDecel, rolling speed at rollDecel, spin at spinDecel (rad/s^2). Stopped (under restSpeed) for recoverDelay s, it rejoins its lane when within rejoinDistance of it and rejoinYawDeg of its heading, blending the offset out over rejoinLength of driving.

parked._: Kerb parked cars (src/city/parking.ts): bodies standing in their slots until struck, then loose like any traffic car but never driving off. Handbrake and park lock hold the wheels, so a shoved one skids to a stop along its heading at rollDecel (m/s^2) instead of rolling.

traffic._kinds: Vehicle kinds: collision size (half length, half width: the body below the mirrors, measured from the models in src/assets/trafficModels.json, which tests hold these to) and mass; share is the spawn mix. The renderer draws each by name from public/traffic/traffic.glb (render/traffic/traffic.ts).

road._readme: Road physics (src/city/roadProfile.ts, read by the terrain and the car): the shape of the surface itself, not a car's tuning, so not in tuningHash. A crown raises a street's middle over its kerbs: the cross slope is the mean rise over run from kerb to centre (a parabola, flat at the middle, twice as steep at the kerb), so a lane's centre sits at about that grade and the car drifts toward the kerb on a straight and leans on the crown through a turn. Junction fans stay flat (layout in config.ts ROAD_PHYSICS). A speed hump is a cosine bump humpHeight high and humpLength long along the street, full height across the lanes and eased off over the outer share of the half width so it never meets the kerb as a step. An expansion joint is a raised cosine lip jointHeight high and jointWidth wide across a deck, every jointSpacing m along it. Metres, rise over run.
road._thump: A wheel over a hump or a joint that compresses faster than thumpMin m/s makes the axle thump (a race event for the sound, value = that speed); the next one comes only after the axle has been quiet for thumpGap s.

cableCar._: The San Francisco cable car (src/sim/cableCar.ts) on sf home seeds: a kinematic body on its timetable that race cars and loose traffic meet through the traffic contact model (collision.ts collideCars) with this mass, so it barely gives and they are shoved. Body (m, kg): a double-ended California Street car, 8.3 m long and 2.6 m wide. It runs at speed (m/s, 15 km/h) on the cable, gripping and letting go at accel (m/s^2).

driftZones._readme: Drift zones (src/sim/driftZones.ts): the monument plaza and the bigger parking lots. Drifting inside one counts drift points scoreMul times (drift mode) and refills nitrous refillMul times as fast (every mode, every car), for at most bonusTime s of drifting and refillCap of a nitrous stage per visit. A visit survives exitGrace s outside; once it ends the zone rests cooldown s before it pays that car again.
driftZones._lots: Parking lots count as zones from this size: depth into the block and frontage length (m), and area (m^2). Smaller lots are too tight to hold a slide.

people._: Pedestrians (src/sim/people.ts): the planned people of the city (src/city/people) as bodies a car hits. mass and radius (kg, m) set the momentum exchange like a prop with anchor 1; below breakSpeed (m/s, closing) a person holds like a short wall; a hit flings the person at flingShare of the car's velocity. sidestep is the stateless dodge every car asks of the people in its path, computed the same in the sim and the shaders.

sidestep._: carHalfWidth and carHalfLength (m) are the car's box as people see it; margin (m) is the room they want beside it; max (m) the furthest a person steps; speed (m/s) how fast they step; lookAhead (m) how far ahead of the car they notice it; behind (m) how far behind its tail they still shy; softSign (m) the lateral distance over which the side chosen blends from one to the other; minSpeed (m/s) the slowest car that asks anyone to move.
